voice-branch-jargon.notes: [EXPIRED-NO-FIELD-HASH] No branch/audit working labels, bean ids, PR/branch references, audit-doc pointers, or agent work-narration found in the .md body or the .ts title.

trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Full read. 'We read binding and decay as parities of one complex object, not as independent predictions' is a substantive contrast — the unification IS the claim.

trap-closing-aphorism.evidence: Closes on the real-part / imaginary-part reading, which is content.

trap-meta-commentary.evidence: Structural description is the function of a section intro.

trap-superlative.evidence: 'The predictions match CODATA and AME data.' is a bare unqualified success claim with no error bar, no observable named and no scope — the strongest sentence in the block and the least supported. The chapter's own numbers do not support it flatly: the sibling table mass-formula-regime-switching-table2-data reports -4.07% on 4He and the jet-tower table reports 0.57-0.86% on 6Li-16O.
trap-superlative.notes: Proposed: name the observables and quote the accuracy, e.g. 'The predicted binding energies track AME to within a few percent for A <= 16 (see the tables below).'

trap-nonspeakable.notes: TWO FINDINGS out of criterion. (1) ABSOLUTE-MASS EXCISION: 'We present the Borromean baryon mass formula, deriving proton and neutron masses from a single common scale.' Under the 2026-08-11 owner ruling, absolute m_p / m_n in MeV is never a framework prediction — it is m_e times a dimensionless ratio, and m_e (CAL-1) sets the MeV scale by fiat. The section intro promises exactly the excised claim. Suggest 'deriving the proton and neutron mass RATIOS from a single common scale' or naming the splitting Delta_pn, which the preceding sentence already does correctly. (2) TERM-COUNT COLLISION: this block says 'the SEVEN-term q-integer mass formula' while markov-trace-frobenius-selection.md and mass-coefficient-shadow-price.md both refer to the SIX-term mass formula / six-term mass identity (thm:six-term-mass-formula-complete, 'Term 4 of the six-term mass identity'). The sibling table mass-formula-regime-switching-table1-data does list seven coefficients, so these are plausibly two different objects — but they are one word apart in the same chapter and nothing distinguishes them for a reader. Worth a naming pass.
